newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hard Rock Cafe in Paris reopens after beef row.
newsitem.headline: Hard Rock Cafe in Paris reopens after beef row.

text.p: The Hard Rock Cafe in Paris reopened on Friday, two weeks after French authorities shut it down after accusing it of importing beef from Britain in defiance of a ban imposed over fears of "mad cow" disease.
"Yes, we're open again. Come and see us soon," a restaurant hostess told callers.
French police closed the Hard Rock Cafe in Paris for two weeks on November 6 after it found 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen hamburger minced beef which it said was illegally imported from Britain.

The European Union banned exports of British beef in March in a bid to protect public health and restore consumer confidence in beef after the British government raised fears that mad cow disease might spread to humans who ate the meat of infected animals.
The restaurant called the ban "totally unjustified", arguing that the minced meat came from Irish cattle, was processed into hamburgers in England at an EU-approved factory and legally exported.
Similar beef turned up at the Hard Rock Cafe in Madrid but authorities there concluded the EU ban had not been violated and took no action.
Though European Commission officials concluded the meat had been legally imported, the French police did not consider the decision binding on French territory, the officials said.
The Paris Hard Rock Cafe is part of a chain of American-style restaurants founded in 1971 and owned by the Rank Organisation Plc.
It has branches around the world including six other EU states: Spain, Denmark, Germany, Belgium, Sweden and Britain.

Hard Rock Cafe, which is headquartered in Orlando, Florida, said the closure of its Paris branch resulted in lost earnings of $650,000 and damaged its international reputation as a supplier of "safe, hygienic, high quality food products."
